description: baseline

n=1024 b60 dense+mixed shapes (~3588us each, 3 of 12 benchmark cases). Profile the n=1024 dense path then attack its dominant cost. The large-n path uses an FP16 blocked-Householder whose trailing-reflector apply (the I-V*T*V^T update) is the GEMM-bound hot loop; on B200 it is leaving the 5th-gen tensor cores under-fed. Restructure the trailing update into wider, fewer tensor-core GEMMs (FP16-in/FP32-accumulate at the 2-CTA M256 atom, larger panel block size to cut panel count / launch count), and overlap panel-factor with the trailing GEMM. Keep the existing ill-conditioning demote-to-geqrf mask intact for held-out correctness. Target beating 3588us on shapes 4 and 8.

OB=128/IB=64 wide outer block: 8 outer blocks vs 16, halving outer-apply+build_Minv launches. Builds+tests pass but diff_correctness_guard FAILS: n1024 mixed (s8) and nearrank (s11) 6/8 inputs wrong. The FP16 trailing apply at w=128 amplifies error past the demote mask thresholds (tuned for w=64). Wider OB needs either FP32 outer apply or a recalibrated mask.

OB=64/IB=64 (single inner sub-panel per outer block, drops PAF inner apply). CRASHES on n1024 with cudaErrorInvalidValue -- the IB=64 (no-inner-rest) path hits an unsupported OV-panel/build_Minv launch config at w=64/m=1024. Also the diff_correctness guard would not run. Confirms: the OB=64/IB=32 two-level geometry is load-bearing (both accuracy AND launch-validity); widening blocks breaks the path. Redirects to the overlap lever (keep geometry, overlap panel with trailing GEMM).

Implemented the brief's headline lever: look-ahead pipelining of the FAR outer trailing apply on a 2nd CUDA stream, overlapping the next outer block's panel factor (panels are 1-CTA/matrix -> ncu 0.41 waves/SM, 19-24% SM throughput, device half-idle). Code BUILDS clean and is structurally correct (double-buffered events, far-private scratch, no buffer race). But validation HARD-FAILS at the banned-construct scan: the GPU MODE leaderboard REJECTS any submission doing work on another CUDA stream ('may result in disqualification'). This is the real remote rule, not a local heuristic. CONCLUSION: stream-based panel/trailing overlap is CATEGORICALLY IMPOSSIBLE for this leaderboard -- the brief's overlap lever cannot be realized. The device-underfill must be attacked WITHIN the default stream (fewer/bigger CTAs per kernel, or a different algorithm), not via concurrency.

n1024: disabled the PAF single-CTA inner-apply fusion (inner_wmma=0, panel_apply_fused=0), routing the inner sub-panel apply to POOLED cuBLAS GEMMs (60 matrices across device) on the hypothesis that single-CTA underfills at B=60. VALIDATES clean. But REGRESSES: geomean 1752.6->1760.6us; n1024 nearrank s11 3550.6->3619.7us. The PAF fusion's saved inner-V HBM round-trip + on-chip WMMA still beats the pooled cuBLAS inner apply even at B=60 -- the comment's claim holds. Rules out 'pool the inner apply' as a lever.

BRIEF EXHAUSTED, NO IMPROVEMENT over the 1752us baseline; the brief's two named levers are both HARD-BLOCKED. (1) OVERLAP panel-with-trailing-GEMM is CATEGORICALLY IMPOSSIBLE: I fully implemented look-ahead 2-stream pipelining (double-buffered events, far-private scratch, race-free, builds clean) but validation HARD-FAILS the banned-construct scan -- GPU MODE leaderboard REJECTS any work on a 2nd CUDA stream ('may result in disqualification'). This is the real remote rule. (2) WIDER PANEL BLOCK is blocked by the load-bearing geometry: OB=128/IB=64 fails diff_correctness (n1024 mixed+nearrank 6/8 wrong -- FP16 w=128 outer apply loses accuracy past the demote-mask thresholds); IB=64 (single-level/block) CRASHES (cudaErrorInvalidValue at OV/build_Minv w=64,m=1024). PROFILE (n1024 dense): panel factor+PAF = 71.6%, trailing nvjet GEMMs only 15.8%, build_Minv 8.3%, +~9% inter-kernel host gap. So the brief's premise (trailing GEMM under-feeds tensor cores) is MISDIRECTED -- the real bottleneck is the SINGLE-CTA-per-matrix PANEL, which ncu shows is latency-bound on the per-column __syncthreads chain at 0.41 waves/SM, 19-24% SM throughput: B=60 matrices launch 60 CTAs onto 148 SMs so HALF THE DEVICE IS STRUCTURALLY IDLE, and the only fix (kernel overlap) is the banned stream path. Disabling the PAF inner fusion to pool the inner apply across the device REGRESSED (1752->1760, s11 3551->3620). HEAD = the PAF-off iteration (validated, benchmarked, slight regression -- do NOT use as a parent; the 1dc4015 baseline is strictly better). RECOMMENDATION: the blocked-Householder path is at its B=60 floor; to beat 3588us at n=1024 needs a DEVICE-FILLING ALGORITHM, i.e. CholeskyQR (Gram=A^TA + Cholesky + Q=A.R^-1, all big batched tensor-core GEMMs that pool 60 matrices across the device) for the well-conditioned majority with the existing demote-mask routing ill-conditioned members to geqrf -- a NEW brief replacing the path, not restructuring its trailing update. CAVEAT to verify in that brief: batched cuSOLVER FP64 Cholesky is slow on B200 (a peer n512 CholeskyQR attempt in this run hit ~26% GPU time on it), and the orhr_col recon contains its own blocked-LU panel that may re-introduce a single-CTA bottleneck -- so the win is not guaranteed and must be measured.

n=1024 b60 (dense/mixed/nearrank, ~3588us each). Your profile proved the single-CTA-per-matrix Householder PANEL is 71.6% and at B=60 only 60 CTAs occupy 148 SMs (0.41 waves/SM, ~20% SM throughput) -- 88 SMs idle during the panel, and streams are banned so cross-matrix overlap is out. Fill the device from INSIDE the kernel: make the panel factorization multi-CTA-per-matrix using Blackwell thread-block clusters (cluster.sync + distributed/cluster shared memory, cudaLaunchKernelEx with cluster dims), so 2-4 cooperating CTAs share each matrix's panel block -- splitting the per-column reflector reduction and the trailing-panel apply across the cluster's CTAs via DSMEM -- giving ~120-240 resident CTAs that fill all SMs. Keep exact FP32/FP16 Householder (no CholeskyQR, no reconstruction) so accuracy is untouched, and keep the demote-to-geqrf mask. Branch off the clean baseline (your dc2db6c2 was a regression).

CLUSTER multi-CTA-per-matrix panel for the n1024 standalone OV panel: 2-CTA thread-block cluster per matrix, m-rows row-split across CTAs, per-column dot/norm reductions combined across the cluster via DSMEM map_shared_rank + cluster.sync. VERIFIED CORRECT: validation PASS, all 3 guards (diff_correctness/invariance/offgrid) clean -- the cluster Householder math is bit-accurate. But REGRESSION: geomean 1752->2126us, n1024 nearrank s11 3551->7658us (2.2x slower). Two causes: (a) 3 cluster.sync/column x32 cols x~16 blocks is heavy; (b) my batched-dot restructure SERIALIZES the bulk trailing apply (for c: for rl) where the original split bulk columns across warps in parallel. Cluster mechanism works (smoke test + validation prove it); the kernel structure needs the bulk apply re-parallelized across warps and fewer cluster syncs. Profiling next.

Cluster panel with WARP-PARALLEL dot+apply (warp-per-column, lanes split rows, warp_reduce) -- matching the single-CTA coop's within-CTA parallelism, plus the row-split across 2 cluster CTAs. VALIDATES PASS (all guards). Cut the iter1 regression hugely: geomean 2126->1849us, n1024 nearrank s11 7658->4339us. But STILL a regression vs the 1752 baseline (s11 baseline 3550): the 2 cluster.sync/column (~1024 cluster-wide barriers/iter at n1024) cost more than the device-fill (0.41->0.81 waves/SM) saves. Need to cut cluster.syncs further or the cluster barrier latency is the floor.

Cluster COLUMN-split panel: each CTA owns INTERLEAVED columns over FULL m rows -> reflector norms+dots are WITHIN-CTA (no cluster reductions), only the finalized reflector column is broadcast: 1 cluster.sync/step (half the row-split's 2). Fixed a reflector inv-double-scaling bug (published raw A[r,j], inv applied in tw -- matches single-CTA). VALIDATES PASS. But SLOWER than row-split iter2: geomean 1849->1994, s11 4339->5951. Causes: (a) bloc=ceil(32/2)=16 columns/CTA but 32 warps -> only 16 warps active in the apply (half idle); (b) only the pivot-owning CTA finalizes each reflector while the other idles at the cl.sync. Fewer barriers did NOT win because warp-utilization + serialization got worse. Both cluster decompositions (row-split 1849, col-split 1994) are CORRECT but REGRESS vs 1752 baseline -- cluster cooperation overhead exceeds the 0.41->0.81 waves/SM device-fill benefit for this fine-grained per-column-dependent panel.

Final cleaned cluster state: removed the cluster smoke-test scaffold (which had verified clusters compile+launch+produce correct DSMEM results on this B200), kept the ROW-split cluster OV panel (the best of the two cluster decompositions). VALIDATES PASS, geomean 1846us. This is the brief's multi-CTA-per-matrix cluster panel, fully built and measured: it FILLS THE DEVICE as intended (ncu: 0.41->0.81 waves/SM) but the per-column cluster.sync barriers net a ~5% regression. Branch HEAD captures the best measured cluster result (not for use as an improvement parent; 1dc4015 baseline is faster).

BRIEF FULLY EXPLORED. Built the brief's multi-CTA-per-matrix cluster panel TWO ways and measured both; both CORRECT but REGRESS vs the 1752 baseline. VERIFIED FACTS: (1) Blackwell thread-block clusters + DSMEM (cudaLaunchKernelEx + cudaLaunchAttributeClusterDimension, cg::this_cluster/map_shared_rank/cluster.sync) COMPILE for sm_100a (CUDA 12.8) and LAUNCH correctly on this B200 (driver 580) -- confirmed by a passing smoke test AND full QR validation. (2) The cluster panel DOES FILL THE DEVICE exactly as the brief predicted: ncu shows waves/SM 0.41->0.81 (the 88 idle SMs are now used, 60->120 resident CTAs). (3) But it is a NET REGRESSION because the panel's per-column serial Householder dependency forces cluster-wide synchronization that costs more than the fill saves. ROW-split (m-rows across CTAs, 2 cluster.sync/column for dot+norm reductions): geomean 1846us, n1024-dense panel kernel 63us->115us/instance (the device-fill cut nothing because cluster.sync >> __syncthreads). COLUMN-split (interleaved cols/CTA, 1 cluster.sync/step, within-CTA reductions): WORSE at 1994us -- bloc=16<32 cols/CTA idles half the warps + owner-only reflector finalize serializes. Iter trace: row-split first cut 2126 (serialized apply) -> warp-parallel 1846 -> col-split 1994. HEAD = b9fcec36 (row-split, cleaned, validated, 1846us) -- do NOT use as an improvement parent; baseline is faster. CONCLUSION for the manager: the multi-CTA cluster idea is sound (it fills the device) but the cluster.sync latency for ~30-60 barriers/panel is the floor for an EXACT per-column Householder panel -- you cannot escape per-column synchronization. To make device-fill pay off you would need an algorithm with COARSER cross-CTA synchronization granularity (sync once per several columns or once per panel), e.g. a communication-avoiding/TSQR-style panel (factor row-block sub-panels independently in separate CTAs, then a small cluster-cooperative reduction tree to combine -- O(log CSIZE) cluster.syncs per panel instead of O(b)), or the CholeskyQR departure (big batched GEMMs that fill the device with NO per-column sync). Both are larger rewrites and distinct briefs.

n=1024 b60 TSQR / communication-avoiding panel. You proved exact per-column Householder has an irreducible O(b) serial-sync critical path: single-CTA panel underfills (0.41 waves), and cluster.sync per column (your brief-1) fills the device but the GPC-wide barrier cost exceeds the fill saving. The escape is COARSER cross-CTA sync granularity. Build a TSQR panel: split the n=1024 column-panel's m rows into K independent row-blocks, factor each row-block's sub-panel in its OWN CTA with ZERO cross-CTA sync (each does a normal local Householder QR of its row-block), then combine the K triangular R-factors pairwise up a reduction tree with only O(log K) cluster-cooperative Householder steps (cluster.sync only at the log K merge levels, not per column). This fills the device with independent sub-panel work AND cuts cross-CTA barriers from O(b) to O(log K), keeping EXACT Householder accuracy (no conditioning risk). Reuse the cluster launch machinery you already validated (cudaLaunchKernelEx + cluster dims work on this B200 sm_100a). Apply the combined reflectors to the trailing matrix as before; keep the demote mask. Profile to confirm waves/SM rises while barrier-stall% falls. Branch off the clean baseline (your b9fcec36 cluster row-split was a regression -- do not build on it).

TSQR-HR cluster panel measured at K=4 (iter1-2) and K=2 (iter3), all VALIDATE PASS (exact Householder). ncu: device is WELL-filled (1.62 waves/SM at K=4, the brief's fill goal exceeded) BUT 71% barrier-stall-bound. Regressions: K=4 2374us, K=2 2159us (baseline 1752). Root cause: (a) my leaf QR is naive column-serial with 2 __syncthreads/column (vs the optimized single-CTA panel's warp-specialized 1-sync/col); (b) the route-2b reconstruction adds an O(b^2)/row triangular forward-solve over ~1000 rows that the baseline does NOT do; (c) B*K CTAs over-subscribe at K=4 (2 waves serialize). Caching U in local smem (iter2) cut DSMEM reads in the solve (2488->2374). The O(log K) MERGE sync IS cheap as predicted, but the leaf's O(b) block-barriers + reconstruction overhead exceed the single-CTA panel. Trying a warp-specialized leaf next.

Final TSQR-HR state (K=2, warp-specialized leaf): VALIDATES PASS (exact Householder), geomean 2153us. ncu (K=2): per-instance 222us (vs single-CTA 63us), 0.81 waves/SM, 64% barrier-stall from merge-idle CTAs (only the low partner works per tree level) + leaf. KEY INSIGHT: the n=1024 panel is LATENCY-bound (a serial chain of ~32 per-column barriers), NOT throughput-bound. Device-fill (clusters brief-1, TSQR brief-2) adds THROUGHPUT but raises per-panel LATENCY (more coordination/barriers), so it addresses the wrong axis. The single-CTA warp-specialized panel's latency (32 cols x 1 barrier) is already near-minimal; every multi-CTA decomposition adds barriers and regresses. Branch HEAD = best TSQR (20c492, regression -- not an improvement parent; baseline faster).

BRIEF FULLY EXPLORED. Built the recommended TSQR-HR communication-avoiding panel END-TO-END and measured it; CORRECT but a consistent REGRESSION. VERIFIED: I implemented a complete TSQR-HR cluster panel -- (LEAF) per-row-block local Householder QR in independent CTAs, (MERGE) pairwise R-factor reduction tree with O(log K) cluster.sync, (RECON) route-2b Householder reconstruction (M=A-S*R no-pivot LU -> Y via a per-row triangular solve; tau via the exact 2/(1+||v||^2) override; R_out=S*R sign-corrected). It VALIDATES PASS on every shape incl n1024 mixed/nearrank diff_correctness -- the CA-QR + HR math is bit-accurate. It FILLS THE DEVICE even better than brief-1 (ncu 1.62 waves/SM at K=4, 0.81 at K=2 -- B*K independent CTAs). The O(log K) MERGE sync IS cheap as the brief predicted. BUT it REGRESSES: K=4 2374us, K=2 2153us (baseline 1752). Iterations: iter1 naive 2488 -> iter2 cache-U-in-smem (kill DSMEM reads in the O(b^2)/row solve) 2374 -> iter3 K=2 2159 -> iter4 warp-specialized leaf (1 sync/col) 2153 (leaf-sync was NOT the bottleneck). ROOT CAUSE (the decisive finding across briefs 0-2): the n=1024 panel is LATENCY-BOUND -- a serial chain of ~32 per-column __syncthreads barriers -- NOT throughput-bound. Device-fill (clusters AND TSQR) adds THROUGHPUT but RAISES per-panel LATENCY via extra coordination: TSQR's merge idles half the CTAs per tree level (64% barrier stall), and the reconstruction adds a per-row triangular solve the baseline doesn't do. The single-CTA warp-specialized panel (32 cols x 1 barrier, ~63us) has near-minimal latency and underfill doesn't matter because the bottleneck is the barrier chain, not SM throughput. So ALL device-fill strategies attack the wrong axis. HEAD = 20c492 (best TSQR, K=2 leaf-opt, validated, 2153us regression -- do NOT use as an improvement parent; 1dc4015 baseline is faster). RECOMMENDATION: stop pursuing n=1024 panel device-fill -- it's latency-bound and at its floor. The remaining real levers for n=1024 are NON-panel: (1) the CholeskyQR departure (replaces the panel ENTIRELY with big batched GEMMs -- the ONLY way to avoid the per-column barrier chain, but squares the condition number so needs the demote-mask + a peer-reported caveat that batched cuSOLVER cholesky is ~26% GPU on B200); or (2) accept the panel floor and squeeze the trailing GEMM / build_Minv / inter-kernel-gap (small, ~1% geomean). The panel itself cannot be made faster by parallelism -- only by a different algorithm with no serial per-column dependency.

n=512 dense (3332us, the largest single cost; device FULL at B=640) trailing-update PRECISION push to FP8/FP4. The serial Householder panel is an irreducible latency wall (3 workers confirmed) -- so the win must come from the PARALLEL trailing GEMM (the FLOP sink, ~50% of n512), not the panel. B200 5th-gen tensor cores run FP8 e4m3 at ~2x and FP4/NVFP4 e2m1 at ~4x the FP16 rate we currently use. Recast the trailing-reflector apply A2 -= V*(T^T*(V^T*A2)) as an FP8-e4m3 (then try NVFP4 e2m1 with per-16-block micro-scaling) tensor-core GEMM with FP32 accumulate, and recover FP32 accuracy with a CHEAP re-orthogonalization/error-correction step: keep the high-order V*A product in FP8/FP4 but add a correction sweep (split-precision residual a la 3xTF32, OR a Newton-Schulz Q(3I-Q^TQ)/2 ortho touch-up on the resulting Q), gated by a per-matrix conditioning probe that falls back to the existing FP16/3xTF32 path on ill-conditioned members. The existing code has NO FP8/FP4 path (only a stale comment claiming 'FP8 far worse' for a DIFFERENT use -- build_Minv inverse -- re-test it for the trailing GEMM, don't trust it). This is the highest-throughput untried lever. Validate the factor+orth gate carefully; FP8/FP4 raw fails cond-2, the correction step is the whole point. Branch off the clean baseline.

FP8-e4m3 single-pass C-=V*Y on the live n512 outer apply via cublasLt. Built end-to-end: verified FP8 cublasLt GEMM (3.7% relerr, layout proven correct via smoke), quant kernels, the gated apply, set_n512_good_flags g_fp8_apply=1. FAILS: cublasLtMatmul returns error 13 (CUBLAS_STATUS_NOT_SUPPORTED) on the real strided-batch B=640 shape (the heuristic found an algo at batch=1 but it fails strided-640 -- likely a stride/output-ld FP8 constraint). MORE DECISIVELY: a built+benchmarked microbenchmark proves FP8 CANNOT win here even if the GEMM worked -- quantizing V+Y to e4m3 (memory-bound, 40M elements) costs ~146us vs the entire FP16 C-=VY GEMM at ~69us, so the FP8 path is ~2-3x SLOWER (quant > GEMM). FP8 wins only when operands are pre-quantized (fused into existing data movement), which the cuBLAS apply can't do (V/Y change per block). The on-chip PAF (50.8%, the real FLOP sink) would avoid the quant pass but FP8 nvcuda::wmma fragments DO NOT COMPILE on sm_100 (verified: incomplete type) -- FP8 there needs hand-written mma.sync PTX.

BRIEF EXPLORED; FP8 trailing-GEMM direction DISPROVEN via build+measure, multiple independent walls. I VERIFIED FP8 works (not trusting the stale comment): built an FP8-e4m3 cublasLt GEMM, proved it correct on this B200 (smoke test relerr 0.037 = expected 3-mantissa-bit precision; torch._scaled_mm agrees at 0.037). Then hit FOUR walls: (1) QUANT OVERHEAD DOMINATES (the decisive one) -- a built+benchmarked microbenchmark on the exact C-=V*Y shape (m512,w64,rest448,B640) shows quantizing V+Y to e4m3 costs ~146us (memory-bound over ~40M elements; even a raw no-amax convert is 38.5us for V alone) vs the entire FP16 C-=VY GEMM at ~69us. So the FP8 path is ~2-3x SLOWER: the per-call quant of operands that CHANGE every block costs more than the compute-bound GEMM it accelerates. FP8 only wins when operands are pre-quantized / quant is fused into existing data movement. (2) The on-chip PAF megakernel (50.8% of n512, the real FLOP sink the brief targets) WOULD avoid the quant pass (quantize in the smem load) -- but FP8 nvcuda::wmma fragments DO NOT COMPILE on sm_100 (verified: 'incomplete type' for matrix_a/b<__nv_fp8_e4m3>). FP8 in the PAF needs hand-written mma.sync.e4m3 PTX -- a research-grade rewrite of the most complex kernel. (3) STREAM BAN COLLISION: cublasLtMatmul REQUIRES a cudaStream_t arg, and the leaderboard's banned-construct scan rejects the substring 'stream'; I worked around it by passing literal 0 (default queue), but it's a landmine. (4) The live strided-batch FP8 GEMM returns cublasLt error 13 (NOT_SUPPORTED) at B=640 (the batch=1 heuristic algo fails strided-640) -- fixable but moot given (1). NET: FP8/FP4 cannot accelerate this trailing apply through cuBLAS (quant-bound), and the only path that could (PAF mma.sync PTX) is a huge high-risk rewrite whose best case is ~0.75% geomean (outer apply is ~25% of n512; PAF FP8 would need the correction step on top). HEAD = clean baseline (no improvement; FP8 code reset). RECOMMENDATION: drop the FP8/FP4 trailing-GEMM lever -- the quant-overhead wall is fundamental for per-block-changing operands. If the manager still wants FP8, the ONLY viable target is the PAF via hand-written mma.sync.e4m3 PTX with fused-in-smem quant + a Newton-Schulz/Ozaki correction -- a multi-day kernel rewrite. Otherwise the n512 remaining levers are the panel (latency-wall, briefs 0-2) or trailing-GEMM micro-tuning.

n=512 b640 PERSISTENT WORK-STEALING scheduler to close the mixed(5023)-vs-dense(3332) 1700us LOAD-IMBALANCE gap. The n512 fused panel+apply megakernel is statically batch->CTA mapped (640 CTAs = batch), measured at 51% occupancy. The mixed/rankdef/clustered batches interleave well-conditioned members (finish fast) with ill-conditioned members (slow: extra Gram-precision passes or demote path). With static mapping, each SM's tail latency = the SLOWEST matrix in its static group, so the fast members' SMs idle waiting at the grid barrier -- THAT is the 1700us mixed-vs-dense gap (it is SCHEDULING, not precision). Convert the launch to a PERSISTENT grid (~one CTA per SM, ~148 CTAs) that pulls the next matrix index off an atomic global counter (atomicAdd), so a freed SM immediately grabs the next unprocessed matrix instead of waiting for its static-group's slowest member. This is INTRA-kernel scheduling -- NO CUDA streams (banned). Attacks the 51% occupancy + load imbalance directly. Validate ALL FOUR n512 b640 variants (dense/mixed/rankdef/clustered) and confirm dense does not regress. Profile to confirm occupancy rises and the mixed tail shrinks. Branch off the clean baseline. Gate sacred; skeptical of dead-end comments.

Persistent work-stealing PAF, two configs measured. persist=2 (296 CTAs, capped): geomean 1926, clustered 2141->2952. persist=6 (640 CTAs=B, no cap, isolates overhead): geomean 1841. Both REGRESS vs 1752 baseline. ROOT CAUSE (built+measured, disproves the brief's premise): (1) the n512 mixed driver already SPLITS good(FP16)/bad(FP32) into separate homogeneous passes, so the PAF only ever processes the well-conditioned GOOD subset -- which is BALANCED (no fast/slow mix to steal across). (2) The PAF is LATENCY-bound (warp-0 serial look-ahead; ncu: 51% occ register-limited, 48% no-eligible-warp), so it wants the FULL static B=640 grid for latency hiding; capping to 296 CTAs REMOVES warps that hide the latency (+85us). (3) The work-stealing atomic + per-matrix sync is pure overhead on a balanced workload (+89us at grid=B). The real 1700us mixed-vs-dense gap is GENUINE FP32-bad-path WORK (nsys: FP16-good 1874us + FP32-bad 1701us, sequential), NOT static-mapping imbalance. Closing it needs OVERLAPPING the good+bad passes -- blocked by the stream ban -- or a unified FP16+FP32 persistent megakernel (merging two precision paths + cutlass GEMMs into one kernel; not feasible).

BRIEF EXPLORED; the persistent-grid load-balancing premise is DISPROVEN by built+measured results. I built a PERSISTENT WORK-STEALING PAF (atomic global counter, capped grid) per the brief, validated CORRECT on all 4 n512 variants, and measured two configs: persist=2 (296 CTAs) geomean 1926 (clustered 2141->2952); persist=6 (640 CTAs=B, isolates overhead) 1841. BOTH REGRESS vs 1752. WHY THE BRIEF'S MODEL IS WRONG (all verified): (1) the n512 mixed driver ALREADY SPLITS good(FP16)/bad(FP32) into separate HOMOGENEOUS passes -- the PAF only ever sees the well-conditioned GOOD subset, which is BALANCED, so there is no fast/slow mix to work-steal across (the split is the load-balancer). (2) The PAF is LATENCY-bound, not imbalance-bound: ncu shows 51% occupancy REGISTER-limited (not CTA-drain) + 48% no-eligible-warp from warp-0's serial look-ahead. A latency-bound kernel wants MORE CTAs to hide latency, so capping the grid (persistent) REMOVES hiding warps (+85us); and the atomic+per-matrix-sync is pure overhead on a balanced load (+89us even at grid=B). (3) nsys decomposition of the 1700us mixed-vs-dense gap: it is GENUINE WORK -- FP16-good 1874us + FP32-bad 1701us run SEQUENTIALLY -- NOT static-mapping imbalance. Closing it requires OVERLAPPING the two passes, which is blocked by the leaderboard stream ban (briefs 0/3 confirmed), or a unified FP16+FP32 persistent megakernel (merging two precision code paths + cutlass GEMMs into one kernel -- not feasible). HEAD = clean baseline (no improvement; persistent code reset, preserved at 0520b0e/7a17e4f). CROSS-BRIEF SYNTHESIS (my briefs 0-4): every structural attack on n512/n1024 keeps hitting the SAME two walls -- (a) the serial Householder PANEL is latency-bound and irreducible (single-CTA optimal; clusters/TSQR/persistent all regress by adding coordination), and (b) the only throughput levers (FP8, kernel overlap) are blocked (FP8 quant-overhead + sm_100 wmma + cublasLt-stream-ban; overlap = stream ban). The frontier here is genuinely hard. RECOMMENDATION: the remaining real levers are NOT scheduling/precision/clustering of the existing kernels -- they are (i) a fundamentally different factorization with NO per-column serial dependency AND no stream/quant dependency (hard to find), or (ii) accept the current ~1752 and micro-tune. The leader's 1292us almost certainly uses an approach outside the blocked-Householder family that this codebase is built on.

ROLL OUT the BREAKTHROUGH to n=4096 (b2, 11418us -- the single LARGEST shape, MOST device-starved, biggest idle-core headroom so the panel-CQR trade pays MOST here). Worker-0 PROVED the non-serial panel works: a narrow b-col panel of a cond-1e4 matrix has panel cond ~1.3, so per-panel block-Gram-Schmidt + CholeskyQR2 orthogonalizer + full-Q orhr_col reconstruction is FP32-safe and replaces the serial per-column __syncthreads Householder chain with tensor-core GEMMs. Your parent commit (W0's milestone 3d0b060d) already contains the VALIDATED panel-CQR2 + _reconstruct_householder machinery -- REUSE it, do not rebuild. n4096 already runs a 1-PASS CholeskyQR + orhr path (B<128 arm); your job: (1) upgrade it to W0's panel-level block-CQR2 (2-pass reortho) approach where it improves accuracy/speed, OR apply the proven non-serial panel to whatever serial-Householder remains in the n4096 path; (2) since the cores are 95% idle at b2, the extra GEMM FLOPs are FREE -- collapse the warp-0 serial critical path.
